small_guidance:
- Add larger-tile autotune configs tuned for M=N=K=4096 on Ada (e.g. BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_K=64 num_warps=8 num_stages=3, BLOCK_M=256/BLOCK_N=128/BLOCK_K=64 num_warps=8 num_stages=3, BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=128/BLOCK_K=64 num_warps=4 num_stages=4) and drop tiny-K configs since K=4096 favors BLOCK_K=64.
- Since K%64==0, M%BLOCK_M==0 and N%BLOCK_N==0 for these shapes, drop the masks on A/B loads in the EVEN_K path (use plain `tl.load(a_ptrs)`); masks force predicated loads and hurt mainloop throughput. Only mask the final store.
- Cache Wt once at __init__ (or first forward) and keep it as a registered buffer to remove the per-call data_ptr check overhead, and ensure scale/shift live on GPU as buffers.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as a split-K or persistent GEMM with fused epilogue: launch one program per SM (persistent loop over (pid_m,pid_n) tiles with swizzle), loading scale/shift/bias once per N-tile and reusing across M-tiles to amortize epilogue overhead.
- Consider running the GEMM in TF32 (`tl.dot(a,b,allow_tf32=True)` on fp32 inputs) — RTX 4090 TF32 throughput is ~2× fp32 and the BN+GELU+ReLU pipeline tolerates the precision; this is the single biggest lever vs cuBLAS which already uses TF32 for fp32 matmul.
- Store the weight pre-transposed as a parameter buffer at init (so B is K-major contiguous for the inner load) and pad N/K to multiples of the chosen BLOCK to eliminate boundary masking entirely.
